Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wuw.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 05 s, 2023 January 18, 2023 MR. JULIETO MANGGASANG Municipal Planning and Development Coordinator Municipality of Carles Province of Iloilo Dear Mr. Manggasang: This has reference to your letter dated November 25, 2022, seeking opinion on the utilization of the 20% Development Fund (DF) to finance Coastal and Fishery Resources Management and related Programs, Projects and Activities (PPAs), thus: I. Procurement and maintenance of Patrol Boats (its engine and body parts); 2. Procurement of Fuel, Oil and Lubricants; 3. Bantay-Dagat Operations which include provision of office supplies, monthly salaries and other allowances of the Bantay-Dagat personnel; 4. Construction and Maintenance of Guard Houses; and 5. Construction and deployment of marine protected areas (MPA) project's boundary markers/buoys. At the outset, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) in its letter dated 24 March 2022 has already settled that it is the LGUs concerned that are in a better position to determine the programs, projects and activities (PPAs) and expenses that may be charged against their respective 20% DFs, as long as the same do not fall within the purview of the list of expenditure items not allowed to be charged against the DF as enumerated in item 3.2.5 of DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 11. The expenditure items that are not allowed to be charged against the 20% DF are as follows: ii. iii. iv. v. Personal Services expenditures, such as salaries, wages, overtime pay, and other personnel benefits; Administrative expenses, such as supplies, meals, representation, communication, water and electricity, petroleum products and the like; Travelling expenses, whether domestic or foreign; Registration fees and other expenses related to the conduct of and participation to trainings, seminars, conferences or conventions; Purchase, maintenance or repair of administrative office' furniture, fixtures, equipment or appliances; and I Revised Guidelines on the Appropriation and Utilization of the Twenty Percent (20%) of the Annual Internal Revenue Allotment for Development Projects" "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

vi. Purchase, maintenance or repair of motor vehicles used for administrative purposes. Relative thereto, herein quoted the pertinent portion of the letter that may guide you on the matter, viz: "Essentially, the said JMC no longer prescribes the specific allowable development projects that may be funded by the LGUs out of their respective 20% DFs. Instead, said JMC sets the general policies and guidelines to be observed by LGUs in identifying and implementing development projects to be funded under the 20% DF, including the prescription of the prohibited expenditure items. It must be noted that one important provision of the JMC is the policy that the development projects that may be included by the LGUs under their respective 20% DFs shall be those that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the efficient and effective local governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people, which is anchored on Section 16 ofRA No. 7160 which provides that, "[w]ithin their respective territorial jurisdictions, local govemment units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. " The general welfare clause under Section 16 of RA No. 7160 and item 3.2.2 of the DBMDOF-DILG JMC essentially cover a wide array of programs, projects, activities (PPAs), or expenses which the LGUs may deem as "necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the efficient and effective local govemance, and [those which arel essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people." Nevertheless, may we emphasize that it is the LGUs concemed that are in a better position to determine the said PPAs and expenses that may be charged against their respective 20% DFs, as long as the same do not fall within the purview of the list of expenditure items not allowed to be charged against the 20% DF .as enumerated in item 3.2.5 of DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1." Accordingly, the LGU concerned is in a better position to determine the programs, projects and activities (PPAs) and expenses that may be charged against their respective 20% DFs, provided that: 1. the same do not fall within the purview of the list of expenditure items not allowed to be charged against the 20% DF as enumerated in item 3.2.5 of DBM- DOF-DILG JMC No. 1; 2. the same is necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the efficient and effective local governance; and 3. the same is essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people. Thus, we are of the view that the requested PPAs, except item no. 3 (Bantay-Dagat Operations which include provision of office supplies, monthly salaries and other allowances of the Bantay-Dagat personnel) may be charged against the 20% DF. Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities (e.g. the Department of Budget and Management) and the courts. Thank you.
